title: A tissue culture infectious dose-derived protocol for testing of SARS-CoV-2 neutralization of serum antibodies on adherent cells
protocol: Aspirate and discard culture medium from Vero cells that are 80%–100% confluent.
Wash the cells gently with PBS.
Add 5 mL Trypsin-EDTA (0.25%) to the flask and return it to 37°C for 5 min incubation.
Deactivate Trypsin-EDTA by adding 5 mL DMEM #1 medium.
Aspirate the cell suspension and transfer it to a 15 mL falcon tube.
Add 5 mL DMEM #1 to the cells in the falcon tube.
Centrifuge cell suspension at 500 × g, at 18°C–22°C, for 5 min.
Resuspend the cells in 5 mL DMEM #1 medium and count them using trypan blue staining method and microscopy.
Set cell concentration to 1×10^5 cells/mL.
Seed 1×10^4 cells (100 μL) per well in flat-bottom 96-well cell culture plates.
Incubate the plates at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 24 h.
Pre-treat serum samples at 56°C for 30 minutes in Eppendorf tubes in a Thermoblock.
Prefill 96-well round-bottom plates with 108 μL DMEM #2 medium in row A and 60 μL DMEM #2 medium in rows B-H.
Transfer 12 μL serum to each well of row A for primary 10-fold dilution.
Mix the samples in row A by aspirating and releasing 60 μL of the samples five times using the multichannel pipette.
Transfer 60 μL of the serum solution from row A to medium-containing wells in row B for a 2-fold dilution.
Replace the pipette tips after transferring serum solution.
Mix the samples in row B by aspirating and releasing 60 μL as above.
Proceed with serial 2-fold dilutions down the plate, replacing the tips between each row.
Discard 60 μL from the last row so that the final volume of each well is 60 μL.
Add serum samples to 96-well plates with culture medium (DMEM #2).
Make two-fold serial dilutions using a multichannel pipette.
Ensure sample ranges from a 10-fold to a 1280-fold dilution before adding virus.
Note that there is an additional two-fold dilution upon adding the virus.
Adjust starting dilution as needed, for example D5 or D100.
Seal the 96-well plates containing diluted serum samples with a lid and plastic foil.
Store the sealed plates at 4°C until further steps are required.
Thaw a frozen aliquot of the virus suspension in the biosafety hood for approximately 15 minutes.
Prepare the targeted concentration of the virus by pipetting an accurate aliquot into a 50 mL falcon tube prefilled with DMEM.
Transfer the entire virus suspension to a reagent reservoir.
Aspirate 60 μL of the virus suspension using a multichannel pipette.
Transfer the suspension to row A on the plates with diluted serum samples.
Repeat the procedure for rows B-H, replacing pipette tips between each row.
Incubate the plates at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 1 hour.
Resuspend serum-virus samples by pipetting up and down twice before transfer.
Transfer 100 μL of serum-virus solution to each well of the plates with adherent Vero cells.
Label the plates and lids for recognition.
Incubate the plates at 37°C in a humidified atmosphere with 5% CO2 for 3 days.
Include non-infected controls.
Include controls with naïve non-neutralizing serum.
Optimize the virus load in each lab and for each viral strain.
Incubate Vero cells with the optimized viral suspension containing 1666.7 PFU/ml for an appropriate period (typically 2-4 days).
Neutralize remaining live virus by treating infected cells with formaldehyde.
Stain infected cells with crystal violet to increase contrast for observation under a microscope or directly on plate.
Observe Vero cell detachment and cytopathic effects after staining.
Add 10% formaldehyde solution to a reagent reservoir.
Transfer 100 μL of formaldehyde solution per well using a multichannel pipette.
Incubate the plates at 18°C–22°C for 15 min.
Discard supernatant into a reagent reservoir using a multichannel pipette.
Wash the plates with 100 μL/well PBS and discard wash solution using the multichannel pipette.
Add 50 μL/well of 1% Gram Hucker’s crystal violet solution using a multichannel pipette.
Incubate the plates at 18°C–22°C for 15 min.
Remove staining solution using a multichannel pipette and discharge waste into a reagent reservoir.
Wash the plates with 100 μL/well PBS, and discard wash solution into the reagent reservoir.
Remove residual washing solution by tapping the plates top-down and gently on a tissue paper.
Disinfect the plates with lids using 70% ethanol in water.
Collect all liquid wastes into 50 mL falcons and close with lids.
Place the stained plates upside down on a luminous board, light table, or similar.
Make photographs of the plates from underneath as well as one matched photograph of the labeled lid for identification of the plate organization.
Dry plates top-down at 18°C–22°C overnight or longer.
